segments.source: 1. From Flood before Market charter and Market charter before New school, infer Flood before New school. 2. Bridge opening is only constrained to be after Flood. There is no stated relation between Bridge opening and Market charter. 3. Therefore the first comparison is forced but the second is underdetermined.
Flood must be before New school. The relative order of Bridge opening and Market charter cannot be determined from the given facts.
A careful reasoner distinguishes what must be true from what merely could be true.
Partial order / directed acyclic graph; use transitive closure and detect incomparable events.
Dates can be used as numbers, but historical labels such as centuries follow explicit conventions.
An institution was founded in 1560 and reorganized in 1589. Use the rule: years 1–100 are the 1st century, 101–200 the 2nd, and so on. Duration is end year minus start year.
Apply the century rule mechanically; do not infer a century from the first two digits alone. Compute elapsed time by subtraction.
How many years passed between the two events? In which centuries did 1560 and 1589 fall?
29 years; 1560 is in the 16th century and 1589 in the 16th century.
Chronological reasoning combines arithmetic with a naming convention; both should be applied explicitly.
Integer arithmetic plus century function c(y)=floor((y−1)/100)+1.
